papers.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
authors: Varun Darshana Parekh, Anusha Devulapally, Sivani Devarapalli, Cassius Henderson, Shimeng Yu, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.21954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. To train the transformer model, we also create a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts perturbed from three representative architectures. On a 150 sample test set, ThermLeT achieves an RMSE of 3.16{\deg}C and an MAE of 2.2

papers.title: KD-DSE: A Knowledge-Driven LLM Framework for Fast Microarchitecture Design Space Exploration
authors: Siqing Fu, Xin Liu, Yuhan Tang, Hanqing Li, Feng Guo
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.22411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Domain-specific architectures have made design space exploration (DSE) a bottleneck of processor design, yet each candidate costs a full simulation, so exhaustive search is out of reach. Surrogate models need thousands of simulations before they predict reliably, and LLM agents that search directly hallucinate, lack cold-start architectural knowledge, and follow a fixed per-round policy. We present KD-DSE, a knowledge- driven LLM framework for fast microarchitecture DSE.
